chunks: Sa'd narrated from Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Majilawayh, from Muhammad ibn Ali al-Sayrafī, who said: Yazid ibn Ishaq Sha'r narrated to us, who said: Harun ibn Hamzah al-Ghanawi al-Sayrafī narrated to us, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a young girl who was divorced and had not yet menstruated, so two months passed for her, then she menstruated. Does she count the two months? He said: 'Yes, and she completes her waiting period by one month.'
I said: Does she complete her waiting period by one menstruation? He said: 'No, but by one month; the end of her waiting period follows the same manner as its beginning.'

The Sheikh (may Allah have mercy on him) said: And if he divorced her before consummation and had not yet specified a dowry for her, then he must provide for her maintenance according to his capacity, as Allah the Exalted said: 'And provide for them in a fair manner, according to the means of the wealthy and according to the means of the poor.'

key_terms.الْمُقْتِرِ قَدَرُهُ: according to the means of the poor
key_terms.الْمُوسِعِ قَدَرُهُ: according to the means of the wealthy
key_terms.جَارِيَةٍ حَدَثٍ: young girl who has not yet reached puberty

ai.seo_question: What is the waiting period (iddah) for a young girl who has not yet menstruated when she is divorced?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the iddah of a young girl (hadiyyah) who has not yet menstruated, establishing that her waiting period is calculated by the passage of time (two months) rather than menstrual cycles, a ruling derived from the principle of analogy with menstruating women. The text further extends this to the requirement of maintenance (mut'ah) for such girls if divorced before consummation, linking the legal obligation directly to the donor's financial capacity as cited in the Quran.
